feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 1 (60 mm span, 16 mm footprint, y = 0.03, kp 6) cut line_loss_events from 1.9 to 1.0 on the slalom and s-bend, but oval progress fell from 0.664 to 0.273, and the mean score fell from 159.7 to 64.6. Iteration 0 (40 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y = 0.05) had the best progress, so the shorter lead is the leading suspect for the collapse. Your design restores y = 0.05 and keeps the span and footprint, so it isolates the lead. max_error stayed at 0.063 to 0.065 m in both iterations, so span and lead alone do not fix off-track excursions. Decide from the next race as follows. If oval progress recovers toward 0.66 and line_loss_events stays near 1, keep the 60 mm span and tune the controller for max_error. If progress stays below about 0.4 while line losses stay near 1, the 16 mm footprint is blurring the centre signal, so move to a 12 mm footprint with the 60 mm span. If line losses rise above about 1.5 again, the wider span is needed and the lead is not the problem.
requested_changes: If progress stays below about 0.4 on the oval with y = 0.05, try sensor_size 0.012 with the same 60 mm span and y = 0.05. Iteration 1 changed footprint and lead together, so the footprint effect has not been isolated.

If progress recovers but max_error stays at 0.063 to 0.065 m on all tracks, try wheel_track 0.10 with the current sensor array. Max_error has stayed at this plateau across iterations 0 and 1, so turn rate is the untested lever.

If line_loss_events fall to 1 and oscillation stays low, try a wider span of x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 with sensor_size 0.008 and y = 0.05. This tests whether a narrower footprint with a wider span holds a graded signal at the tape edge.
